prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1120; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after the policyholder reported being struck while turning left at an intersection. The claimant is the driver of the other vehicle and is represented by counsel, and all further contact is being routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the initial statements from both drivers and the police report. Both accounts describe the same sequence of events, with the other vehicle entering the intersection as the policyholder completed the left turn.

Entry 3: Obtained scene photographs and spoke with two independent witnesses, who both confirm the collision occurred as described. Nothing in their accounts conflicts with the other driver's version.

Entry 4: Inspected the vehicle damage. The damage is mostly consistent with the impact described and lines up with the points of contact shown in the scene photos.

Entry 5: Verified coverage. The driving policyholder lives with the named insured and qualifies as a covered household member. Nothing suggests the damage predates the start of the policy.

Entry 6: Requested prior claims history for the vehicle and found no earlier damage on record that would overlap with this loss.

Entry 7: Received the claimant's medical records through counsel. The reported knee injury fits well with the type and force of a side impact of this kind.

Entry 8: Reviewed the treatment history. The care followed a typical course, with frequency of visits tapering as the claimant improved and returned to normal activity.

Entry 9: Checked prior medical records for the same body area and found no earlier injury or complaint involving the knee.

Entry 10: Spoke with the claimant through counsel. The account given matches what was described in every earlier conversation, with no material differences in the details.

Entry 11: Noted that the exact seating position of the claimant at impact is not fully clear from the available records. This is being documented, though it does not currently change the assessment of the injury.

Entry 12: Current status: liability and injury evaluation are substantially complete. File is pending final review and settlement discussions with counsel.
